sentences.text: In order to prove their cases, petitioner has examined an independent witness namely Saroj Kumar as PW2.

From his testimony recorded before the Tribunal as well as statement under section 161 Cr PC as recorded during investigation in the criminal case trial Ex. PW2/2, it comes to fore that he was a witness to the spot and a primary witness at point of hearing.

He has stated that he was going on his motorcycle and on hearing of loud noise coming from his backside, when he had looked back, he had seen that the offending vehicle had slipped on the road and both driver and pillion rider had fallen down.

He has clearly stated that he had found that both of them were drunk at that time and he assumed that there was at fault on the part of the motorcycle driver in driving his vehicle, as there was no other vehicle on the road and hence there was no question of _____________________________________________________________ MACP No.928/19;
involvement of any other vehicle in the accident.
MLC of the injured as well as R-1 is part of DAR and clearly reflects that smell of alcohol was present at the time of their medical examination.
There was lapse on the part of IO as he did not get the driver medically examined on the point of blood alcohol level.

From FIR and other criminal case record, it can been seen that offending vehicle was in possession of R-1 / driver and hence it can be opined that he was the driver of the offending vehicle and there is no reason for any other assumption.

The copy of notice u/s 133 M.V. Act and reply thereto is on record and part of DAR and reflects that R-2 had stated in the reply that he had given the motorcycle to his brother in law Somen for the purpose of driving and at the time of accident, Somen was driving the same.
R-1 has not disputed this fact and no written statement has been filed by him.

It is further seen that while in his testimony before the Tribunal, PW2 did not elucidate on the point of driver being drunk or there being any other vehicle at the spot when he immediately looked back after hearing noise of falling of the vehicle, it is seen that these facts are mentioned in his statement Ex. PW2/2, relied on by him during his deposition.

PW2 is not an eye witness of accident but eye witness to the circumstances surrounding the accident in the immediate aftermath and an eye witness on the point of turning back and seeing the vehicle i.e. motorcycle fallen on road and both the riders on road and he has not stated anything to draw an inference regarding there being anything odd to arouse suspicion regarding the involvement of any other vehicle in the accident.

PW2 is also a witness to the res gestae on the point of res ipsa loquitor, as r o u t i n e l y

10. It is not disputed that after detailed investigation of the case, respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted under Sections 279/338/304-A IPC for causing fatal injury to deceased Samit Saha.
The FIR was registered on the same day.
Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and charge-sheet has also been filed against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.

Reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case titled as Shabina v. Satvir & Ors. MAC. APP. 980/17 dated 24.01.2020,
wherein Hon'ble Delhi High Court observed that in so far as FIR has been registered, criminal case has been initiated against driver of offending vehicle and vehicle was seized, the requirement of proving the preponderance of probability of accident having been caused by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle has been established.

ISSUE NO. 2:
13.
Next it is to be seen, whether terms and conditions of insurance policy were breached as R-1 was not having driving licence and was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.

It is to be seen that charge-sheet attached with the DAR reflects that the driver / R-1 was also booked for offence u/s 3 / 181 M.V. Act for not having driving licence and further R- 2 was booked for offence u/s 5/181 M.V. Act for permitting R-1 to drive the offending motorcycle without having a valid DL.
It is seen that respondents did not file any written statement in their defence.

Further, R-3 has examined R3W1 who has proved on record R3W1/1 i.e. the insurance policy of the offending vehicle which clearly reflects that the insurance policy had a specific driver clause, whereby the insurance company's liability was limited to the case where the driver had valid driving licence on the date of accident, which was not the case here.
In the statement given by R- 1 before the Tribunal on 06.0.2020, he stated that "I was not holding driving licence at the time of accident".
Hence, it is clear that there was a breach of the terms and conditions of insurance policy as R-1 did not have valid driving licence.
Further, as far as the issue of R-1 being under influence of liquor is concerned

,
sadly no sufficient evidence has come on record in this regard. R-1 was not subjected to alcometer Swapan Shaha vs Somen on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134703031/

In the absence of any medical finding regarding the blood alcohol level of R-1, it cannot be concluded that he was under the influence of liquor or had consumed beyond permissible limits.
ISSUE NO.3 14.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners in the claim case are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

16. In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:death case Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.

Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier
) death case
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

There is nothing to suggest that Samit Shaha was giving tuition.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that income of the deceased may be considered as per minimum wages of a matriculate in Delhi and has mentioned so in the written submissions.

LIABILITY 31.

As discussed above, issue no. 2 is already decided in favour of R-3 /insurer /Shri Ram GIC on the point of R-1 not having driving licence at the time of accident, and thus, the terms and conditions of insurance policy were breached by R-1, it can be concluded that respondents No. 1 and 2 committed breach of fundamental terms and conditions of insurance policy.
In view of this, the insurance company would be entitled for recovery of compensation payable to the petitioners from the respondents No.1 and 2.
The liability of the respondents No. 1 and 2 would be joint and several.
RELIEF 32.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.27,68,000/- (rupees twenty seven Lakhs sixty eight Thousands Only) to the petitioners along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.3/ insurance company and the same shall be recoverable by insurance company from R-1 and R-2.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
33. The apportionment of the award amount shall be decided only after deposit of award amount.
34. With these observations, the claim petition is disposed of.
Copy of the Award be given dasti to the parties free of cost.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012,
Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530,
Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
From his testimony recorded before the Tribunal as well as statement under section 161 Cr PC as recorded during investigation in the criminal case trial Ex. PW2/2, it comes to fore that he was a witness to the spot and a primary witness at point of hearing.
PW2 is not an eye witness of accident but eye witness to the circumstances surrounding the accident in the immediate aftermath and an eye witness on the point of turning back and seeing the vehicle i.e. motorcycle fallen on road and both the riders on road and he has not stated anything to draw an inference regarding there being anything odd to arouse suspicion regarding the involvement of any other vehicle in the accident.
The FIR was registered on the same day.
Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and charge-sheet has also been filed against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.
Hence, it is clear that there was a breach of the terms and conditions of insurance policy as R-1 did not have valid driving licence.
In the absence of any medical finding regarding the blood alcohol level of R-1, it cannot be concluded that he was under the influence of liquor or had consumed beyond permissible limits.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners in the claim case are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
16. In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
The instant claim petition has been filed by two petitioners, who are father (Swapan Saha) and mother (Amita Saha) of deceased.
Thus, for the purpose of ascertaining the dependency of the deceased, petitioners are considered dependents on the deceased.
As discussed above, the deceased was considered to be 20 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.44,000/-, 16,500/- and Rs.16,500/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Thus, claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,21,000/- (44,000x2+16,500+16,500) under this head.

Thus, both the petitioners i.e. father and mother of the deceased in the instant case shall be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.27,68,000/- (rounded off) only.
Petitioners shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
LIABILITY 31.
As discussed above, issue no. 2 is already decided in favour of R-3 /insurer /Shri Ram GIC on the point of R-1 not having driving licence at the time of accident, and thus, the terms and conditions of insurance policy were breached by R-1, it can be concluded that respondents No. 1 and 2 committed breach of fundamental terms and conditions of insurance policy.
In view of this, the insurance company would be entitled for recovery of compensation payable to the petitioners from the respondents No.1 and 2.
The liability of the respondents No. 1 and 2 would be joint and several.
RELIEF 32.
This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.27,68,000/- (rupees twenty seven Lakhs sixty eight Thousands Only) to the petitioners along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.3/ insurance company and the same shall be recoverable by insurance company from R-1 and R-2.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
33. The apportionment of the award amount shall be decided only after deposit of award amount.
34. With these observations, the claim petition is disposed of.
Copy of the Award be given dasti to the parties free of cost.
